name: Trash Talk
label: Deathwish
lede: A Sacramento hardcore band that Steve Albini mixed, Keith Morris sang for and Odd Future signed, all while running its own label.

eras.title: Sacramento, in a hurry
eras.text: Trash Talk formed in Sacramento in 2005 and moved fast: a demo, a split, a first full-length and a spot on a Deathwish imprint within about two years. The sound was crossover thrash and hardcore played at skatepark speed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trash Talk (band) · Wikipedia: Lee Spielman
years.h: Trash Talk forms in Sacramento
years.p: [[Lee Spielman|f183f98c-117b-445d-a836-f2c141174e92]] and [[Spencer Pollard|e0dfbf99-c4b6-4add-a4b6-42144402d5bf]] start the band in 2005. A demo comes out on Sell Our Souls Records the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the band to 2005 in Sacramento, with Spielman on vocals and Pollard on bass and backing vocals. The first release was a self-titled 7-inch on Sell Our Souls.

years.h: Split 7-inch with Bay Area band Steel Trap
years.p: The split comes out on Spiderghost Pressgang. It is the band's second release in about a year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lee Spielman · The FADER · Metal Insider
years.h: Guitarist Garrett Stevenson joins
years.p: [[Garrett Stevenson|c136c559-192c-4874-a48e-ee91095bf1c1]] becomes the guitarist in 2007, the year of the debut album Walking Disease on Rumble Records.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Stevenson as a member from 2007. He went on to run the band's business side: The FADER called him the de facto manager, and Metal Insider's interview names him as the member who handles most Trash Talk Collective operations.

years.h: Malfunction Records, a Deathwish imprint, signs them
years.p: The band lands on Malfunction, an imprint of Deathwish Inc., and records the Plagues EP.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Malfunction signing to 2007 and lists the Plagues EP in 2008. The band toured heavily with Cruel Hand in this stretch.

eras.title: Chicago, Albini, and their own label
eras.text: After the Deathwish compilation, the band went to Chicago to record with Steve Albini, then started Trash Talk Collective to put out its own records. The label was run by the band's circle from then on.

years.h: Plagues... Walking Disease on Deathwish
years.p: The 17-track compilation pairs the six-song Plagues 7-inch with the earlier Walking Disease. Exclaim reviewed it on April 24, 2008.
years.xp: Exclaim's Keith Carman heard Cryptic Slaughter, D.R.I. and Discharge in it, plus a [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]-style edge, and called the production crisp.

years.src: Discogs · Metal Insider · Wikipedia: Trash Talk (band)
years.h: Self-titled LP, recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio
years.p: The band records in Chicago and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] mixes the album at Electrical Audio. It comes out on Trash Talk Collective, with a 250-copy European vinyl pressing on Reflections Records.
years.xp: Discogs credits the recording to Electrical Audio in Chicago, with Albini mixing and Nick Zampiello mastering at New Alliance East. Spielman later said working with a friend on the next record was far more relaxed than Albini's strict schedule.

years.big: Their own label, their own rules
q: Releasing our own records is something that we have always wanted to do.
years.h: Off Deathwish, onto Trash Talk Collective
years.p: The band leaves the Malfunction/Deathwish arrangement and starts Trash Talk Collective to release its own records.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the band left Deathwish Inc. to start the label. Stevenson handles most of its business, with friends helping while the band is on tour.

Spielman told Metal Insider the label came from a long-held wish.

years.h: Keith Morris sings on the "East of Eden" 7-inch
years.p: The Black Flag, Circle Jerks and OFF! singer guests on "East of Eden", released by Trash Talk Collective.
years.xp: The single pairs "East of Eden" with "Son of a Bitch". The same year the band played a live session for BBC Radio 1, and the UK label Hassle Records put out the two-disc compilation Shame.

eras.title: Explode
eras.text: Eyes & Nines made them a name outside hardcore: a magazine cover, a Kerrang award, and long tours across the UK, Europe and the US. Fans of both the Sacramento scene and the hip-hop crowd were paying attention.

years.h: Eyes & Nines is recorded at Big Game Lodge
years.p: Joby J. Ford of The Bronx produces. Greg Hetson plays extra guitar and Matt Caughthran adds vocals on several songs.
years.xp:
The band announced the record in February through its blog and offered a pre-order with the "Explode" single and video. Wikipedia lists a digital release around May 18 and physical copies in June, and reports a Metacritic score of 83. Rock Sound gave it 10 out of 10 and Pitchfork 7.8.

The Icelandic volcano eruption in April cost the band tour dates, Spielman said.

years.cap: Trash Talk on the cover of The FADER, issue 70
years.h: Trash Talk get The FADER cover
years.p: The magazine's October 2010 issue puts the band on the cover. A November feature, "Trash Talk Explode", follows.
years.xp:
The FADER described the band as four members who had "replaced love with business", with Stevenson running the label. It also reported that the band had just won Kerrang's award for Best International Newcomer.

Pollard and Stevenson told the magazine about being Black musicians in a hardcore band; Stevenson recounted a bouncer refusing him entry to his own sold-out show.

years.h: 85 days on the road, and a Florida club owner sends bikers
years.p: At a Clearwater, Florida show a speaker is damaged and the owner demands payment and calls biker friends to the parking lot.
years.xp: Thrasher's interview places this on an 85-day tour through the UK, Europe and the US with The Bronx, Iron Age, Cold World and Sick of It All. The band left without injury and without paying.

years.h: Awake 7-inch on True Panther Sounds
years.p: A five-song EP released October 11, 2011, a year after the band's FADER cover.

years.cap: Odd Future and Trash Talk at the Roxy
years.src: Beats Per Minute · Wikipedia: Radicals (song) · NPR
years.h: Trash Talk back Odd Future on "Radicals" at the Roxy
years.p: On December 23, 2011 the band plays behind [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]] at the Roxy in Los Angeles. Odd Future sometimes performed "Radicals" with Trash Talk backing them.
years.xp: The link came from touring. NPR later called them "your favorite rapper's favorite punk band", and reported the band toured with [[Tyler, the Creator|f6beac20-5dfe-4d1f-ae02-0b0a740aafd6]] and Action Bronson.

eras.title: The punks on Odd Future Records
eras.text: Odd Future Records signed them, and Trash Talk became the label's first non-hip-hop act. Two albums followed, then a drummer change that took in a former Mars Volta player.

years.h: Odd Future Records signs Trash Talk
years.p: On May 30, 2012 the band joins [[Odd Future|519336c2-f5a3-4137-a88e-58fecc604575]]'s label as its first act outside the hip-hop collective and its first non-hip-hop artist.
years.xp: AllMusic and Wikipedia both call the band the first non-hip-hop signing. The move put a Sacramento hardcore band in front of an Odd Future crowd, and 119 then reached No. 15 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, Wikipedia says.

years.h: 119 features Tyler, the Creator and Hodgy on "Blossom & Burn"
years.p: [[Hodgy|76600f02-c090-4d15-8782-680cde16bd98]] and Tyler guest on track 6 of a 14-song, 22-minute album released October 9, 2012.
years.xp: "F.E.B.N." came out as a single with a video on August 30. 119 was the first Odd Future Records release without an Odd Future member. Pitchfork gave it 7.4, and NME and Under the Radar were positive.

years.h: Former Mars Volta drummer Thomas Pridgen joins
years.p: The Mars Volta's Thomas Pridgen is announced as the band's drummer on May 13, 2013. Drummer Sam Bosson is not mentioned.
years.xp: Metal Injection and Lambgoat reported the move; The PRP noted there was no word on what happened to Bosson. Last.fm's summary instead names Devan Bentley as drummer from November 2013, and Wikipedia's infobox gives Pridgen 2014, so the timeline of drummers is unclear.

years.h: No Peace is 16 songs in 28 minutes
years.p: Alchemist produces "Amnesiatic" and "Reprieve" and King Krule appears on "Stackin' Skins". It came out May 27, 2014.
years.xp: Consequence gave it a C+, calling it a short blast of classic hardcore with occasional hip-hop and electronic touches.

eras.title: Still going
eras.text: The band kept releasing records and added a new guitarist. Squalor pushed them toward a producer's input for the first time.

years.h: Tangle EP on Trash Talk Collective
years.p: The band's first release in two years, put out on its own label.

years.h: Band announces its next record is finished
years.p: On October 18, 2019 the band says the new album is done. The release that follows is the Squalor EP.

years.h: Kenny Beats produces Squalor
years.p: The five-song EP came out June 5, 2020. It was Kenny Beats' first full project with a band, with live drums and guitars.
years.xp: Stevenson told Louder that it was the first time the band worked with a producer who shaped the record throughout, not just engineered. Thomas Pridgen returned on drums to record it.

years.h: "Something Wicked" short film scored with Squalor
years.p: The dark short reimagines Edgar Allan Poe's "William Wilson" in snowy middle America. It was released October 14, 2020.
